Work in the regime of
[[def-nondegenerate-root-of-unity-level-one-hecke-regime]]. Fix a partition
$\mu$, put $d=|\mu|$, $\alpha=\operatorname{cont}(\mu)$, and let $K(\mu)$ be
the $F$-span of the Murphy elements $m_{S,T}$ of
[[def-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-cell-and-schur-modules]] with
$S,T$ standard tableaux of a multipartition strictly dominating $\mu$; by
[[thm-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-basis-is-cellular]] $K(\mu)$ is a
two-sided ideal of $H^\Lambda_d$ and $z_\mu:=m_{t^\mu t^\mu}+K(\mu)$ is
defined. Define the (level-one) **cell/Specht module**
$$S(\mu):=H^\Lambda_d\,z_\mu\subseteq H^\Lambda_d/K(\mu),$$
a LEFT $H^\Lambda_d$-module lying in the block $H^\Lambda_\alpha$.

For every standard $\mu$-tableau $T$
([[def-young-tableau-standard-tableau-and-shape]]) fix a reduced decomposition
$w_T=s_{r_1}\cdots s_{r_m}$ of the associated permutation and put
$z_T:=T_{w_T}z_\mu$, $v_T:=\psi_{w_T}z_\mu$ in the Khovanov--Lauda presentation
of `def-type-a-cyclotomic-specialization-of-the-qg-klr-algebras`. For a
removable $i$-node $A$ of a partition $\lambda$
([[def-removable-and-addable-nodes-of-a-partition]]) define
$$d_A(\lambda):=\#\{\text{addable }i\text{-nodes strictly below }A\}-\#\{\text{removable }i\text{-nodes strictly below }A\}$$
(equivalently in the level-one symmetric residue convention of the regime) and
define the **degree** of a standard tableau inductively by
$\deg(\varnothing):=0$ and, for $d>0$,
$\deg(T):=\deg(T_{\le d-1})+d_A(\mu)$ where $A$ is the node of $T$ containing
$d$.

The definition asserts, and
`thm-graded-specht-module-has-homogeneous-tableau-basis` on this page proves,
that $\{v_T:T\in\operatorname{Std}(\mu)\}$ is a homogeneous $F$-basis of
$S(\mu)$ making it a graded $R^\Lambda_\alpha$-module whose $q$-character is
$\operatorname{ch}_qS(\mu)=\sum_Tq^{\deg T}i_T$; forgetting the grading
recovers the ungraded cell module. **Convention.** This is the LEFT Murphy cell
module, obtained from the right cellular datum by $h\cdot m=m h^*$. Forgetting
its grading, `thm-dj-bridge-murphy-cell-is-the-same-shape-specht-dual`
identifies it with the star-contragredient dual of the same-shape
independently defined ordinary Dipper--James Specht module $P(\mu)$. Separately,
`thm-dj-bridge-ordinary-specht-is-the-signed-conjugate-murphy-cell` gives
$S(\mu)\cong P(\mu')^{\theta}$ after the same left-module conversion. These are
two proved module comparisons, not the identification of an untwisted conjugate
module. The sign pullback may change ordinary residue content from $-\alpha$ to
$\alpha$; these ungraded comparisons do not assert homogeneity of the ordinary
form or of a raw Hecke sign automorphism in the fixed transported grading. The
labelling of simples by $e$-restricted or $e$-regular partitions is NOT asserted
here; it is determined by the head-classification theorem later on this page.

No choice is used in the definition.

For $H_n$ in
[[def-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-cell-and-schur-modules]] over
the universal Laurent parameter ring, the elements $m_{st}$ indexed by all
$\ell$-multipartitions of $n$ and standard tableaux $s,t$ of that shape are a
basis and a dominance-cellular datum:
$$m_{st}^*=m_{ts},\qquad m_{st}h\equiv\sum_vr_{(t,v)}(h)\,m_{sv}\pmod{H^{>\lambda}},$$
with coefficients $r_{(t,v)}(h)$ independent of $s$. The higher spans are
actual two-sided ideals. Every commutative specialization with unit parameters
inherits the cellular basis; in particular the arbitrary-field finite-$e$
nondegenerate charged specializations ($q_H\ne1$) and the LM deformation DVR retain it. The specialization $z=1$ here is the multiplicative presentation with $T_i^2=1$, not the additive degenerate cyclotomic Hecke algebra. The universal
rank is supplied independently by
[[lem-universal-cyclotomic-hecke-ordered-monomials-form-a-basis]], not by a
primitive-block classification.

For every commutative ring $R$, every $q\in R^\times$, and every partition
$\lambda\vdash n$ with row symmetrizer $m_\lambda=x_\lambda$, put
$m_{st}:=T_{d(s)}^*m_\lambda T_{d(t)}$ for standard $\lambda$-tableaux $s,t$,
where $d(t)\in D_\lambda$ is the element with $t^\lambda\cdot d(t)=t$. Then:

1. $\{m_{st}:\lambda\vdash n,\ s,t\in\operatorname{Std}(\lambda)\}$ is an
$R$-basis of $H$ (the **Murphy basis**), and $m_{st}^*=m_{ts}$.

2. The $R$-spans $I^{\unrhd\lambda}$ of $\{m_{uv}:\mu\unrhd\lambda\}$ and
$I^{\rhd\lambda}$ of $\{m_{uv}:\mu\rhd\lambda\}$ are two-sided ideals of $H$
(dominance order), and $I^{\unrhd\lambda}/I^{\rhd\lambda}$ is free with basis
the classes of $\{m_{st}:s,t\in\operatorname{Std}(\lambda)\}$.

3. The **Murphy cell module**
$C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda):=M(\lambda)/(M(\lambda)\cap I^{\rhd\lambda})$ is free
with basis $\{m_t:=x_\lambda T_{d(t)}+I^{\rhd\lambda}:t\in\operatorname{Std}(\lambda)\}$
and satisfies the **cell law**: for $h\in H$ and standard $s,t$,
$$m_{st}h\equiv\sum_{v\in\operatorname{Std}(\lambda)}r_v\,m_{sv}\pmod{I^{\rhd\lambda}},\qquad r_v\in R,$$
with coefficients $r_v$ independent of $s$.

4. There is a unique $R$-bilinear **Murphy form** $G_\lambda$ on
$C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)$ with
$m_{us}m_{tv}\equiv G_\lambda(m_s,m_t)m_{uv}\pmod{I^{\rhd\lambda}}$; it is
symmetric, associative in the sense
$G_\lambda(m_sh,m_t)=G_\lambda(m_s,m_th^*)$, and its radical is a submodule of
$C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)$.

5. The basis, the ideals, the cell law and the form are compatible with every
base change.

The proof also supplies the auxiliary identities used by the comparison:
$\tau(T_w)=\delta_{w,1}$ defines a trace with
$\tau(T_u^*T_v)=\delta_{u,v}q^{\ell(u)}$ (step 1.3); for a composition
$\alpha$ and the partition $\beta$ obtained by sorting its parts,
$x_\alpha=T_dx_\beta T_d^{-1}$ with a block-reordering permutation $d$
(step 2.2); and for the Garnir composition $\alpha$ at a node of $\rho$,
$x_\rho\sum_{d\in S_\alpha\cap D_\rho}T_d
=\sum_{v\in S_\rho\cap D_\alpha}T_v^*x_\alpha$ (step 2.3).
The block-reordering and Garnir data are specified in those steps.

In particular $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)$ is finite free of rank
$f^\lambda=|\operatorname{Std}(\lambda)|$. No choice principle is used.

Retain English Young diagrams, an $l$-multicomposition $\mu$ of $d$, its
diagram, and the row-reading initial standard tableau $t^\mu$, in which
$1,2,\dots,d$ appear in order along the successive rows from top to bottom
([[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]); for a single
component this is the standard tableau of
[[def-young-tableau-standard-tableau-and-shape]]. A $\mu$-tableau $T$ is a
placement of $1,\dots,d$ in the nodes of $\mu$. It is **row-strict** if its
entries increase from left to right in every row of every component, and
**standard** if it is row- and column-strict. The group $S_d$ acts on tableaux
by its action on entries, and for a $\mu$-tableau $T$ the permutation $w_T$ is
defined by $w_Tt^\mu=T$. The **strong Bruhat order** on tableaux is
$$S\le_BT\quad:\Longleftrightarrow\quad w_S\le w_T$$
in the Bruhat order of [[def-bruhat-order-on-the-symmetric-group]], identified
with its one-based realization as in
[[lem-bruhat-order-basic-properties-for-permutations]]. We write $S\unlhd T$
for $S\le_BT$ and $S\lhd T$ for strict order; the separately declared meaning
of $\unrhd$ on partitions ([[def-dominance-order-on-partitions]]) is not
reused for tableaux. On row-strict $S,T$ the order $\unlhd$ is equivalent to
the prefix-shape comparison
$$\operatorname{sh}(S^{\le a})\unrhd\operatorname{sh}(T^{\le a})\quad\text{for every }a,$$
where $T^{\le a}$ erases the nodes occupied by entries $>a$ and
$\operatorname{sh}$ records the resulting row lengths read in row-reading
order; this row-sequence dominance is distinct from the weak Bruhat order and
must not be reversed. The transposition criterion is
$$S=(a_1\,b_1)\cdots(a_m\,b_m)T$$
with $a_n<b_n$ and $b_n$ occupying an earlier row-reading node than $a_n$ in
$(a_{n+1}\,b_{n+1})\cdots(a_m\,b_m)T$ for each $n$.

For entries $r,s$ of one component define $r\to_Ts$ if they lie in the same row
and $s$ is strictly to the right of $r$; $r\downarrow_Ts$ if they lie in the
same column and $s$ is strictly below $r$; and $r\nearrow_Ts$ if $s$ is
strictly above and strictly right of $r$ (south-west is the reverse of
$\nearrow_T$). A **weak Bruhat graph edge** $T\xrightarrow{r}S$ requires both
tableaux standard, $S=s_rT$, and $r$ occupying an earlier row-reading node
than $r+1$. Equivalently $r+1\nearrow_Tr$, or $r$ lies in an earlier component
than $r+1$. In particular a same-row or same-column swap is NOT a standard
edge. A **terminal path** is a directed path in this graph, and $T$ is
$(r_1,\dots,r_m)$-**terminal** if there are standard tableaux
$S_1\xrightarrow{r_1}S_2\xrightarrow{r_2}\cdots\xrightarrow{r_m}T$.

The **Garnir belt** at a node $(a,b,n)$ with $(a+1,b,n)$ also a node of $\mu$
consists of the nodes $(a,c,n)$ for $b\le c\le\mu_a$ and the nodes
$(a+1,g,n)$ for $1\le g\le b$. The **Garnir tableau** of shape $\mu$ at
$(a,b,n)$ is the unique maximal standard $\mu$-tableau in the order $\unlhd$
among the standard $\mu$-tableaux agreeing with $t^\mu$ outside the
$(a,b,n)$-Garnir belt; it equals $t^\mu$ in the degenerate case
$b=1=\mu_a$. A **horizontal brick** is a string of consecutive entries along
same-row right arrows. For the vertical exceptional-prefix and terminal assertions assume that
$\mu$ is a multipartition; the rank, prefix-order and row-sorting assertions
allow multicompositions. The following source facts are retained with these
exact conventions and are proved below: the transposition criterion and the
prefix-shape criterion; the row-strictness of a vertical consecutive swap and
its exceptional-prefix comparison; agreement outside the Garnir belt for
tableaux below a Garnir tableau; and the four terminal alternatives for a
horizontal or vertical consecutive pair, the last alternative being $t^\mu$
for a horizontal pair and the corresponding Garnir tableau for a vertical
pair. No choice.

Let $\lambda\vdash n$ and let $[\lambda]$ be its Young diagram
([[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]). A **tableau of shape
$\lambda$**, or $\lambda$-tableau, is a bijection
$$t:[\lambda]\longrightarrow\{1,2,\dots,n\}.$$
We write $t(i,j)$ for the entry of $t$ in the node $(i,j)$, and we display $t$
as the diagram $[\lambda]$ with each node carrying its entry. Thus a tableau
places each of the numbers $1,\dots,n$ in exactly one node of $[\lambda]$. For
$\lambda=\varnothing$ the diagram is empty and the empty map is the unique
tableau of shape $\varnothing$, the **empty tableau**. The **shape** of a
tableau $t$ is the partition $\lambda$ with $t:[\lambda]\to\{1,\dots,n\}$,
which is determined by $t$ because $[\lambda]$ determines $\lambda$.

**Standard tableaux.** A tableau $t$ of shape $\lambda$ is **standard** if its
entries strictly increase along rows and down columns, that is, if
$$t(i,j)<t(i,j+1)\quad\text{whenever }(i,j),(i,j+1)\in[\lambda],$$
$$t(i,j)<t(i+1,j)\quad\text{whenever }(i,j),(i+1,j)\in[\lambda].$$
The empty tableau is standard, because both conditions are vacuous, and it is
the unique standard tableau of shape $\varnothing$. Following the classical
notation we write $f^\lambda$ for the number of standard $\lambda$-tableaux.

**The left action on tableaux.** For $\sigma\in S_n$ and a $\lambda$-tableau
$t$, define
$$(\sigma\cdot t)(i,j):=\sigma\bigl(t(i,j)\bigr)\qquad\bigl((i,j)\in[\lambda]\bigr).$$
Since $t$ is a bijection onto $\{1,\dots,n\}$ and $\sigma$ is a bijection of
$\{1,\dots,n\}$, the map $\sigma\cdot t$ is again a bijection
$[\lambda]\to\{1,\dots,n\}$, hence again a $\lambda$-tableau, and
$\mathrm{id}\cdot t=t$, $\sigma\cdot(\tau\cdot t)=(\sigma\tau)\cdot t$ for all
$\sigma,\tau\in S_n$: the rule is a left action of $S_n$ on the set of
$\lambda$-tableaux. For every $\sigma\in S_n$ the row sets of $\sigma\cdot t$
are the images under $\sigma$ of the row sets of $t$, and the column sets of
$\sigma\cdot t$ are the images under $\sigma$ of the column sets of $t$.

In the situation of
[[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]], define
$d^A(\lambda)$ for an ADDABLE $i$-node $A$ to be the number of addable
$i$-nodes strictly ABOVE $A$ minus the number of removable $i$-nodes strictly
ABOVE $A$. Define the codegree of a standard tableau $T$ by
$\operatorname{codeg}(\varnothing):=0$ and
$\operatorname{codeg}(T):=d^A(\mu^A)+\operatorname{codeg}(T_{\le d-1})$, where
$A$ is the node containing $d$ and $\mu^A=\mu\setminus A$. Define the defect of
a residue content $\alpha\in Q_+$ by
$\operatorname{def}(\alpha):=(\Lambda_0,\alpha)-(\alpha,\alpha)/2$ (the
symmetric form of [[def-cyclic-affine-type-a-cartan-datum]]). Then for every
partition $\mu$ with content $\alpha$ and every standard $\mu$-tableau $T$:

1. $d_A(\mu)+d^A(\mu^A)=d_i(\mu)+1$ where $i$ is the residue of the removable
node $A$ and
$d_i(\mu)=\#\{\text{addable }i\text{-nodes of }\mu\}-\#\{\text{removable }i\text{-nodes of }\mu\}$;

2. $d_i(\mu)=(\Lambda_0-\alpha,\alpha_i)$;

3. $\operatorname{def}(\alpha)=\operatorname{def}(\alpha-\alpha_i)+d_i(\mu)+1$;

4. $\deg(T)+\operatorname{codeg}(T)=\operatorname{def}(\alpha)$;

5. removing a brick does not change the codegree: if
$m\to_Tm+1\to_T\cdots\to_Td$ and $S=T_{\le m-1}$, then
$\operatorname{codeg}(S)=\operatorname{codeg}(T)$ whenever (i) $m,\dots,d$
occupy nodes in the first row of the first component of $T$, or (ii)
$d-m+1=e$ (the quantum characteristic).

No choice is used.

In the situation of
[[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]]:

1. If $T\xrightarrow{\,r\,}S$ (i.e. both tableaux are standard, $S=s_rT$, and
$r$ occupies an earlier row-reading node than $r+1$, as in
[[def-tableau-domination-order-garnir-tableaux-and-bricks]]), then
$\deg(S)-\deg(T)=-a_{i_ri_{r+1}}$, where $i_T=(i_1,\dots,i_d)$ and $a$ is the
Cartan matrix of the regime.

2. More generally, if $w_T=s_{r_1}\cdots s_{r_m}$ is a reduced decomposition,
then $\deg(T)-\deg(t^\mu)=\deg\bigl(\psi_{r_1}\cdots\psi_{r_m}e(i_{t^\mu})\bigr)$
in the grading of [[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]].

3. If $T$ is the $(a,b)$-Garnir tableau with entry $r$ in the node $(a,b)$, and
$S$ is a standard $\mu$-tableau with $S\lhd T$ and $i_S=i_{s_rT}$, then
$\deg(S)-\deg(T)=-a_{i_ri_{r+1}}$ as well.

No choice is used.

Let $F,q,e,I,\Lambda,\lambda_i$ be as in
[[def-affine-and-cyclotomic-type-a-hecke-algebras]]
([[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]],
[[def-cyclic-affine-type-a-cartan-datum]]). On the cyclic affine type-A Cartan
datum take the normalized symmetrizers $d_i=1$ and define the **type-A KLR
datum** $Q^{\mathrm A}$ by
$$Q^{\mathrm A}_{ii}=0,\qquad Q^{\mathrm A}_{ij}=1\quad\text{if }a_{ij}=0,$$
$$Q^{\mathrm A}_{i,i+1}(u,v)=v-u,\qquad Q^{\mathrm A}_{i+1,i}(u,v)=u-v\qquad(e\ge3),$$
$$Q^{\mathrm A}_{01}(u,v)=Q^{\mathrm A}_{10}(u,v)=-(u-v)^2\qquad(e=2).$$
Write $R_\alpha$ for the resulting generalized KLR algebra over $F$
([[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]],
[[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]]) and $R^\Lambda_\alpha$ for
the standard cyclotomic quotient of
[[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]] (monic first-strand
relations $x_1^{\lambda_{i_1}}e(\nu)=0$).

**The specialization dictionary.** Put $y_r:=x_r$ and $\psi_r:=-\tau_r$. With
these normalizations, the relations (1.6)–(1.15) of the source hold in
$R^\Lambda_\alpha$, and conversely the quotient presented by those relations
is the same algebra; in other words $R^\Lambda_\alpha$ is the sign-modified
cyclotomic Khovanov–Lauda algebra of the source for the cyclic quiver of
quantum characteristic $e$. The verification of the dictionary is elementary
and is recorded here so that no hidden convention is imported:

1. **(Q1)–(Q4).** Non-adjacent pairs have $a_{ij}=0$ and
   $Q^{\mathrm A}_{ij}=1$, homogeneous of degree $0$. For an adjacent pair
   $(i,i+1)$ with $e\ge3$ one has $b_{ij}=a_{ij}=-1$, and $v-u$ is homogeneous
   of degree $2=-2b_{ij}$ with nonzero extremal coefficients of
   $u^{-a_{ij}}=u$ and $v^{-a_{ji}}=v$; the opposite orientation is the
   transpose, so (Q2) is built into the two formulae. For $e=2$ the pair
   $\{0,1\}$ has $a_{01}=a_{10}=-2$ and $b_{01}=-2$, and $-(u-v)^2$ is
   symmetric, homogeneous of degree $4=-2b_{01}$, with top coefficient $-1\ne0$.
2. **Dot sliding.** Relation (1.8) comes from $\tau_re(i)=e(s_ri)\tau_r$;
   relations (1.12)–(1.13) reduce to the dot-sliding constants
   $\tau_ax_a-x_{a+1}\tau_a=e(\nu)$ and
   $\tau_ax_{a+1}-x_a\tau_a=-e(\nu)$ on equal colours, whose sign changes to
   the source's constants $+1$ under $\psi=-\tau$.
3. **Quadratic and braid relations.** Relation (1.14): equal colours give
   $\tau^2=Q_{ii}=0$; non-adjacent colours give $\tau^2=1=e(i)$; a forward
   arrow gives $\tau^2=v-u$, evaluated at $(y_r,y_{r+1})$ as
   $y_{r+1}-y_r$; a backward arrow gives $y_r-y_{r+1}$; the $e=2$ double edge
   gives $(y_{r+1}-y_r)(y_r-y_{r+1})$. Relation (1.15): the divided-difference
   numerator
   $\bigl[Q^{\mathrm A}(x_a,x_{a+1})-Q^{\mathrm A}(x_{a+2},x_{a+1})\bigr]/(x_{a+2}-x_a)$
   equals $\pm1$ in the two single-edge cases with $i_{r+2}=i_r$, equals
   $y_r+y_{r+2}-2y_{r+1}$ in the $e=2$ double-edge case, and vanishes
   otherwise; the global sign $\psi=-\tau$ matches the source's three cases.
   The product order is explicit: the source difference is
   $\psi_r\psi_{r+1}\psi_r-\psi_{r+1}\psi_r\psi_{r+1}$, which under
   $\psi=-\tau$ equals the native reversed-word difference
   $\tau_{r+1}\tau_r\tau_{r+1}-\tau_r\tau_{r+1}\tau_r$; for
   $Q=-(u-v)^2$ the displayed quotient is $u+w-2v$. Thus no braid-order sign
   is suppressed, also in characteristic two.

Degrees of products are read on the successive permuted colour pairs as in
[[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]]. This definition introduces
no new basis, trace or primitive-block assertion, and uses no choice
principle.

derivations.claim: **Ungraded straightening and triangularity.** The cellular Murphy straightening in [F1], in its left version, expresses $z_U$ for any tableau $U$ as a sum of standard $z_S$ with $w_S\le w_U$; row sorting is passage to the parabolic minimal representative, hence lowers Bruhat order; each Garnir replacement raises prefix dominance, hence strictly lowers Bruhat order by the row-boundary rank-count equivalence proved in [F2]. The standard $z_T=m_{T,t^\mu}+K(\mu)$ are independent because they are distinct surviving cellular basis elements, and they span the cyclic module by that straightening. The initial-vector calculation in the Definition gives $e(i_{t^\mu})z_\mu=z_\mu$ and $y_az_\mu=0$. In the fixed BK presentation, $\psi_re(i)=(T_r+P_r(i))Q_r(i)^{-1}e(i)$, where $Q_r(i)$ has invertible constant term. Expand a reduced product and slide dots right using the mixed relations: the result is a sum $T_{r_{a_1}}\cdots T_{r_{a_b}}f(y)z_\mu$ over subwords, and the full-subword coefficient is a product of nonzero constants $Q_r(i)^{-1}(0)$. Rightmost dots evaluate at zero. The Hecke quadratic relation and the Bruhat subword criterion reduce each proper subword to $T_uz_\mu$ with $u<w_T$, so Murphy straightening gives $v_T=a_Tz_T+\sum_{S\lhd T}a_Sz_S$, with $a_T\ne0$ for standard $T$. This proves a basis for each selected reduced-word family and also straightens every nonstandard $v_U$ into standard $v_S$ with $S\unlhd U$.

**Filtered KLR word calculus before a grading on the module.** A dot moved through a crossing becomes the permuted dot plus a scalar term only for equal residues; moving all dots to the right thus deletes crossings in every scalar error. Two reduced words are connected by Coxeter moves. A distant move is exact; a length-three braid changes the product to a polynomial in dots times the remaining word, deleting the three crossings of that braid. A nonreduced word is shortened by bringing a repeated simple reflection together through these moves and replacing its square by its KLR quadratic polynomial. Induction on word length, using the deletion/subword criterion, therefore writes every error as $\psi_uf(y)e(i_{t^\mu})$ with $u<w_T$ and preserves its algebra degree. Acting on $z_\mu$ kills positive-degree rightmost dot monomials. Combined with step 1.1 this gives, without presupposing module homogeneity: reduced-word changes have only $v_S$ with $S\lhd T$; $y_av_T$ has only $S\lhd T$; and if $a,a+1$ share a row or column, $\psi_av_T$ has only $S\lhd T$ and $i_S=s_ai_T$. For the last assertion first straighten below $s_aT$ and use the exceptional-prefix comparison of [F2] to get $S\unlhd T$; equality is excluded because adjacent same-row or same-column boxes have distinct residues for $e\ge2$. Weight support follows directly from $\psi_ae(i)=e(s_ai)\psi_a$ and commuting dots.

**The simultaneous induction.** Assign degree $\deg T$ to the selected basis $v_T$. Prove together, for $m\ge0$, (a) word-change errors at standard tableaux of length at most $m$ have degree $\deg T$, and (b) all dot and crossing actions at standard tableaux of length at most $m-1$ have their prescribed degrees. The base $m=0$ has the unique length-zero tableau $t^\mu$ and no action assertion. For (a), a nontrivial braid error has at most $m-3$ crossings after step 2.1 and the same algebra degree as the original reduced word. Act on $z_\mu$ successively with the at most $m-3$ crossings of each shortened term, expanding after each action in the ungraded selected standard basis. Step 1.1 bounds every appearing standard-tableau length by the number of crossings so far, and step 2.1 gives the corresponding bound after straightening a nonreduced product. Thus before every action the standard-basis lengths are at most $m-4$, and the already proved action assertion (b) applies. No standardness of an arbitrary subword tableau is assumed. By [F3] the algebra degree plus $\deg(t^\mu)$ is $\deg T$. Strict-order straightening and weight support in step 2.1 therefore give exactly the difference formula (2). A sequence of braid moves gives it for any two words.

**Dot actions in the induction.** At $\ell(T)=m-1$ write $v_T=\psi_av_U$ with $\ell(U)=m-2$; word changes only add shorter vectors of the same degree by step 3.1. Slide $y_r$ past $\psi_a$. The main term is $\psi_ay_{s_a(r)}v_U$, and the possible scalar error is $\pm v_U$ at equal crossing colors. The dot action at $U$ is homogeneous by induction and, by step 2.1, is supported on lengths strictly below $m-2$, so applying $\psi_a$ to all its basis terms is covered by induction. The mixed relation is homogeneous, so both the main term and the scalar error have degree $\deg T+2$. When $T=t^\mu$, the dot is zero. This proves every dot assertion at length $m-1$.

**Crossing actions at standard swaps.** If $s_rT$ is standard and has length $m$, the word $s_rw_T$ is reduced, so the word-change assertion just proved at length $m$ and the weak-edge identity in [F3] give degree $\deg T-a_{i_ri_{r+1}}$. If $s_rT$ instead has length $m-2$, write $v_T=\psi_rv_{s_rT}$ up to shorter same-weight same-degree errors. Apply $\psi_r$: the main term becomes $Q_{i_ri_{r+1}}(y_r,y_{r+1})v_{s_rT}$, and the other terms are crossing actions at strictly shorter tableaux. Those actions are covered by induction and the dot polynomial by step 4.1 and induction. Homogeneity of the quadratic relation gives the required degree also for this case.

**Crossing actions at a horizontal or vertical pair.** The four terminal alternatives of [F2] complete the crossing induction. For a distant terminal edge $t$, write $v_T=\psi_tv_U$ up to shorter homogeneous errors, with $|t-r|>1$. Commute $\psi_r$ past $\psi_t$. The action $\psi_rv_U$ is supported strictly below $U$ by step 2.1 because the horizontal or vertical relation persists, so both successive actions are already covered by induction and their degree is the homogeneous product degree. For a two-edge terminal alternative write $v_T=\psi_{r\pm1}\psi_rv_U$ up to shorter homogeneous errors, where $\ell(U)=m-3$ and $r\pm1,r\pm1+1$ are horizontal or vertical in $U$. The braid relation rewrites $\psi_r\psi_{r\pm1}\psi_rv_U$ as $\psi_{r\pm1}\psi_r\psi_{r\pm1}v_U$ plus the homogeneous dot correction. By step 2.1 the first action on the rewritten word is supported strictly below $U$, so all remaining actions use strictly shorter lengths and induction; step 4.1 handles the dot correction. The horizontal terminal base is $T=t^\mu$: step 2.1 makes $\psi_rv_T=0$. The vertical terminal base is the Garnir tableau. Here step 2.1 gives only $v_S$ with $S\lhd T$ and $i_S=s_ri_T$, and the Garnir exchange formula in [F3] gives $\deg S=\deg T-a_{i_ri_{r+1}}$ for every such term. This proves (b), completing the simultaneous induction without assuming the homogeneity being proved.

**Grading, character and independence.** The weight identity in step 2.1 and the action degrees established in steps 4.1–6.1 show that the vector-space grading is a module grading. Zero images belong to the stated homogeneous components; a degree is asserted only for a nonzero vector. Step 3.1 makes every change of selected reduced words a unitriangular basis change within each weight and degree, so it preserves the graded subspaces while individual $v_T$ may change. Finally the homogeneous basis yields $\operatorname{ch}_qS(\mu)=\sum_Tq^{\deg T}i_T$ and the construction used exactly the original ungraded left Murphy cell. Every selection is finite and requires no choice principle.

Work in the regime of
[[def-nondegenerate-root-of-unity-level-one-hecke-regime]]. Fix a partition
$\mu$, put $d=|\mu|$, $\alpha=\operatorname{cont}(\mu)$, and let $K(\mu)$ be
the $F$-span of the Murphy elements $m_{S,T}$ of
[[def-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-cell-and-schur-modules]] with
$S,T$ standard tableaux of a multipartition strictly dominating $\mu$; by
[[thm-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-basis-is-cellular]] $K(\mu)$ is a
two-sided ideal of $H^\Lambda_d$ and $z_\mu:=m_{t^\mu t^\mu}+K(\mu)$ is
defined. Define the (level-one) **cell/Specht module**
$$S(\mu):=H^\Lambda_d\,z_\mu\subseteq H^\Lambda_d/K(\mu),$$
a LEFT $H^\Lambda_d$-module lying in the block $H^\Lambda_\alpha$.

For every standard $\mu$-tableau $T$
([[def-young-tableau-standard-tableau-and-shape]]) fix a reduced decomposition
$w_T=s_{r_1}\cdots s_{r_m}$ of the associated permutation and put
$z_T:=T_{w_T}z_\mu$, $v_T:=\psi_{w_T}z_\mu$ in the Khovanov--Lauda presentation
of `def-type-a-cyclotomic-specialization-of-the-qg-klr-algebras`. For a
removable $i$-node $A$ of a partition $\lambda$
([[def-removable-and-addable-nodes-of-a-partition]]) define
$$d_A(\lambda):=\#\{\text{addable }i\text{-nodes strictly below }A\}-\#\{\text{removable }i\text{-nodes strictly below }A\}$$
(equivalently in the level-one symmetric residue convention of the regime) and
define the **degree** of a standard tableau inductively by
$\deg(\varnothing):=0$ and, for $d>0$,
$\deg(T):=\deg(T_{\le d-1})+d_A(\mu)$ where $A$ is the node of $T$ containing
$d$.

The definition asserts, and
`thm-graded-specht-module-has-homogeneous-tableau-basis` on this page proves,
that $\{v_T:T\in\operatorname{Std}(\mu)\}$ is a homogeneous $F$-basis of
$S(\mu)$ making it a graded $R^\Lambda_\alpha$-module whose $q$-character is
$\operatorname{ch}_qS(\mu)=\sum_Tq^{\deg T}i_T$; forgetting the grading
recovers the ungraded cell module. **Convention.** This is the LEFT Murphy cell
module, obtained from the right cellular datum by $h\cdot m=m h^*$. Forgetting
its grading, `thm-dj-bridge-murphy-cell-is-the-same-shape-specht-dual`
identifies it with the star-contragredient dual of the same-shape
independently defined ordinary Dipper--James Specht module $P(\mu)$. Separately,
`thm-dj-bridge-ordinary-specht-is-the-signed-conjugate-murphy-cell` gives
$S(\mu)\cong P(\mu')^{\theta}$ after the same left-module conversion. These are
two proved module comparisons, not the identification of an untwisted conjugate
module. The sign pullback may change ordinary residue content from $-\alpha$ to
$\alpha$; these ungraded comparisons do not assert homogeneity of the ordinary
form or of a raw Hecke sign automorphism in the fixed transported grading. The
labelling of simples by $e$-restricted or $e$-regular partitions is NOT asserted
here; it is determined by the head-classification theorem later on this page.

No choice is used in the definition.

Keep the notation of
[[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]]; the vectors
$v_T=\psi_{w_T}z_\mu$ may a priori depend on the chosen reduced decompositions
$w_T=s_{r_1}\cdots s_{r_m}$. Then:

1. For every $\mu$-tableau $T$ one has $v_T=\sum_{S\unlhd T}a_Sz_S$ with
$a_T\ne0$ when $T$ is standard; hence the standard vectors form a basis of
$S(\mu)$ triangular with respect to the standard basis $\{z_T\}$ of
[[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]].

2. If $w_T=s_{r_1}\cdots s_{r_m}=s_{t_1}\cdots s_{t_m}$ are two reduced
decompositions of the same $w_T$, then
$\psi_{r_1}\cdots\psi_{r_m}z_\mu-\psi_{t_1}\cdots\psi_{t_m}z_\mu=\sum_{S\lhd T,\ i_S=i_T,\ \deg S=\deg T}a_Sv_S$;
in particular the grading on $S(\mu)$ defined by $\deg(v_T):=\deg(T)$ is
independent of the choices.

3. For every $r$ the vectors $e(i)v_T$, $y_rv_T$ and $\psi_rv_T$ lie in
the prescribed homogeneous components; when nonzero their degrees satisfy
$$e(i)v_T=\delta_{i,i_T}v_T,\qquad \deg(y_rv_T)=\deg(y_r)+\deg(T),\qquad \deg(\psi_rv_T)=\deg(\psi_re(i_T))+\deg(T).$$
Hence $S(\mu)$ is a graded $R^\Lambda_\alpha$-module with homogeneous basis
$\{v_T\}$ and $q$-character
$\operatorname{ch}_qS(\mu)=\sum_{T\in\operatorname{Std}(\mu)}q^{\deg T}i_T$;
forgetting the grading recovers the ungraded cell module of
[[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]].

No choice beyond the finite selections of reduced decompositions is used; the
resulting graded isomorphism class is independent of them by (2).

Use the standard graded cyclotomic quotient of
[[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]], and keep the conventions
fixed there: the cyclotomic relation is imposed on the FIRST strand and
cyclotomic induction appends strands on the RIGHT. Fix $\beta\in Q_+$ and a
color $i$; put
$$A:=R^\Lambda(\beta),\qquad B:=R^\Lambda(\beta+\alpha_i),\qquad e:=e(\beta,i),$$
where $e(\beta,i)=\sum_{\nu\in I^\beta}e(\nu i)\in R(\beta+\alpha_i)$ is the
idempotent of [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]]
supported on the sequences ending in $i$.

**The right-append corner homomorphism.** Right append defines a
$k$-algebra homomorphism
$$\iota_i:A\longrightarrow eBe,\qquad 1_A\longmapsto e,\quad e(\nu)\longmapsto e(\nu i),\quad x_a\longmapsto x_ae,\quad \tau_a\longmapsto\tau_ae ,$$
sending each old dot or crossing to the same-named generator multiplied by
the endpoint idempotent $e$, at the same position in the first $|\beta|$ strands of $R^\Lambda(\beta+\alpha_i)$ and
each old idempotent to the longer idempotent obtained by appending $i$. It is
a graded homomorphism of degree zero: each generic relation (1)-(7) of
[[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] is preserved
under right append, and the first-strand cyclotomic generator of $A$ maps to
the first-strand cyclotomic generator of $B$, so the cyclotomic relation is
preserved and $\iota_i$ is well defined on the quotient. The unit is sent to
the corner unit $e$, not to a global unit of $B$; it is **not** asserted that
$\iota_i$ is injective, and $e$ is allowed to be zero.

**The functors.** On graded left modules define
$$F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}(M):=Be\otimes_A M,\qquad E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}(N):=eN,$$
the tensor over the graded balanced tensor product of
[[def-graded-balanced-tensor-product-and-homogeneous-hom]] and the idempotent
restriction of the graded $B$-module $N$
([[def-graded-ring-module-bimodule-and-internal-shift]]). Both are additive
$k$-linear functors between the graded module categories, they preserve
degree-zero maps, and they extend to direct sums over the root degrees
$\beta\in Q_+$.

**Adjunction, weights and shifts.** Evaluation at $e$ identifies
$\operatorname{HOM}_B(Be,N)$ with $eN$ by the degree-zero tensor--Hom
adjunction, giving $F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}\dashv E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$ with its
actual grading. The functor $F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$ increases ROOT degree by
$\alpha_i$, taking modules at root $\beta$ to modules at root
$\beta+\alpha_i$, and decreases the module weight $\Lambda-\beta$ by
$\alpha_i$; restriction does the reverse. Both composites are endofunctors at
a fixed root degree. Grading shifts satisfy
$F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}(M\{r\})\cong F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}(M)\{r\}$ and
$E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}(N\{r\})\cong E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}(N)\{r\}$, using the
internal shifts of [[def-graded-ring-module-bimodule-and-internal-shift]].

**Ungraded monic deformations.** For a general monic
specialization $a_j(u)$ the quotient $R^\Lambda_a(\beta)$ of
[[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]] carries no grading, and
the same formulas define the ungraded functors $F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$ and
$E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$; no graded statement is asserted on that branch.

**Status of further structure.** Exactness, preservation of projectives and a
shifted second adjunction are theorems below, not part of this definition; in
particular no unshifted right adjunction $E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}\dashv
F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$ is asserted here, and the explicit shift of the second
adjunction is supplied by the coherent-biadjunction lemma of this page. This
definition uses no choice.

Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]]. For $ eta,\gamma\in Q_+$ put $e( eta,\gamma):=\sum_{
u\in I^{ eta},
u'\in I^{\gamma}}e(
u\ast
u')\in R( eta+\gamma)$, where $
u\ast
u'$ is concatenation; this is an idempotent. The block inclusions $R( eta)\hookrightarrow R( eta+\gamma)$, $r\mapsto r\otimes1$ and $R(\gamma)\hookrightarrow R( eta+\gamma)$, $s\mapsto1\otimes s$ combine into an injective $k$-algebra map $R( eta)\otimes_kR(\gamma)	o R( eta+\gamma)$ whose image is the separated-block subalgebra of the corner $e( eta,\gamma)R( eta+\gamma)e( eta,\gamma)$; the inclusion generally is proper; in the diagram calculus it is horizontal concatenation of diagrams. **Induction** and **restriction** are the functors on graded left modules
$$\mathrm{Ind}_{ eta,\gamma}(M oxtimes N):=R( eta+\gamma)e( eta,\gamma)\otimes_{R( eta)\otimes_kR(\gamma)}(M\otimes_kN),\qquad \mathrm{Res}_{ eta,\gamma}L:=e( eta,\gamma)L,$$

For a partial flag $ eta= eta_1+\cdots+ eta_r$ the iterated functors are defined by iteration, and the parenthesization-independent identification is the one consumed below.

Let $F,q,e,I,\Lambda,\lambda_i$ be as in
[[def-affine-and-cyclotomic-type-a-hecke-algebras]]
([[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]],
[[def-cyclic-affine-type-a-cartan-datum]]). On the cyclic affine type-A Cartan
datum take the normalized symmetrizers $d_i=1$ and define the **type-A KLR
datum** $Q^{\mathrm A}$ by
$$Q^{\mathrm A}_{ii}=0,\qquad Q^{\mathrm A}_{ij}=1\quad\text{if }a_{ij}=0,$$
$$Q^{\mathrm A}_{i,i+1}(u,v)=v-u,\qquad Q^{\mathrm A}_{i+1,i}(u,v)=u-v\qquad(e\ge3),$$
$$Q^{\mathrm A}_{01}(u,v)=Q^{\mathrm A}_{10}(u,v)=-(u-v)^2\qquad(e=2).$$
Write $R_\alpha$ for the resulting generalized KLR algebra over $F$
([[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]],
[[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]]) and $R^\Lambda_\alpha$ for
the standard cyclotomic quotient of
[[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]] (monic first-strand
relations $x_1^{\lambda_{i_1}}e(\nu)=0$).

**The specialization dictionary.** Put $y_r:=x_r$ and $\psi_r:=-\tau_r$. With
these normalizations, the relations (1.6)–(1.15) of the source hold in
$R^\Lambda_\alpha$, and conversely the quotient presented by those relations
is the same algebra; in other words $R^\Lambda_\alpha$ is the sign-modified
cyclotomic Khovanov–Lauda algebra of the source for the cyclic quiver of
quantum characteristic $e$. The verification of the dictionary is elementary
and is recorded here so that no hidden convention is imported:

1. **(Q1)–(Q4).** Non-adjacent pairs have $a_{ij}=0$ and
   $Q^{\mathrm A}_{ij}=1$, homogeneous of degree $0$. For an adjacent pair
   $(i,i+1)$ with $e\ge3$ one has $b_{ij}=a_{ij}=-1$, and $v-u$ is homogeneous
   of degree $2=-2b_{ij}$ with nonzero extremal coefficients of
   $u^{-a_{ij}}=u$ and $v^{-a_{ji}}=v$; the opposite orientation is the
   transpose, so (Q2) is built into the two formulae. For $e=2$ the pair
   $\{0,1\}$ has $a_{01}=a_{10}=-2$ and $b_{01}=-2$, and $-(u-v)^2$ is
   symmetric, homogeneous of degree $4=-2b_{01}$, with top coefficient $-1\ne0$.
2. **Dot sliding.** Relation (1.8) comes from $\tau_re(i)=e(s_ri)\tau_r$;
   relations (1.12)–(1.13) reduce to the dot-sliding constants
   $\tau_ax_a-x_{a+1}\tau_a=e(\nu)$ and
   $\tau_ax_{a+1}-x_a\tau_a=-e(\nu)$ on equal colours, whose sign changes to
   the source's constants $+1$ under $\psi=-\tau$.
3. **Quadratic and braid relations.** Relation (1.14): equal colours give
   $\tau^2=Q_{ii}=0$; non-adjacent colours give $\tau^2=1=e(i)$; a forward
   arrow gives $\tau^2=v-u$, evaluated at $(y_r,y_{r+1})$ as
   $y_{r+1}-y_r$; a backward arrow gives $y_r-y_{r+1}$; the $e=2$ double edge
   gives $(y_{r+1}-y_r)(y_r-y_{r+1})$. Relation (1.15): the divided-difference
   numerator
   $\bigl[Q^{\mathrm A}(x_a,x_{a+1})-Q^{\mathrm A}(x_{a+2},x_{a+1})\bigr]/(x_{a+2}-x_a)$
   equals $\pm1$ in the two single-edge cases with $i_{r+2}=i_r$, equals
   $y_r+y_{r+2}-2y_{r+1}$ in the $e=2$ double-edge case, and vanishes
   otherwise; the global sign $\psi=-\tau$ matches the source's three cases.
   The product order is explicit: the source difference is
   $\psi_r\psi_{r+1}\psi_r-\psi_{r+1}\psi_r\psi_{r+1}$, which under
   $\psi=-\tau$ equals the native reversed-word difference
   $\tau_{r+1}\tau_r\tau_{r+1}-\tau_r\tau_{r+1}\tau_r$; for
   $Q=-(u-v)^2$ the displayed quotient is $u+w-2v$. Thus no braid-order sign
   is suppressed, also in characteristic two.

diagram, and the row-reading initial standard tableau $t^\mu$, in which
$1,2,\dots,d$ appear in order along the successive rows from top to bottom
([[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]); for a single
component this is the standard tableau of
[[def-young-tableau-standard-tableau-and-shape]]. A $\mu$-tableau $T$ is a
placement of $1,\dots,d$ in the nodes of $\mu$. It is **row-strict** if its
entries increase from left to right in every row of every component, and
**standard** if it is row- and column-strict. The group $S_d$ acts on tableaux
by its action on entries, and for a $\mu$-tableau $T$ the permutation $w_T$ is
defined by $w_Tt^\mu=T$. The **strong Bruhat order** on tableaux is
$$S\le_BT\quad:\Longleftrightarrow\quad w_S\le w_T$$
in the Bruhat order of [[def-bruhat-order-on-the-symmetric-group]], identified
with its one-based realization as in
[[lem-bruhat-order-basic-properties-for-permutations]]. We write $S\unlhd T$
for $S\le_BT$ and $S\lhd T$ for strict order; the separately declared meaning
of $\unrhd$ on partitions ([[def-dominance-order-on-partitions]]) is not
reused for tableaux. On row-strict $S,T$ the order $\unlhd$ is equivalent to
the prefix-shape comparison
$$\operatorname{sh}(S^{\le a})\unrhd\operatorname{sh}(T^{\le a})\quad\text{for every }a,$$
where $T^{\le a}$ erases the nodes occupied by entries $>a$ and
$\operatorname{sh}$ records the resulting row lengths read in row-reading
order; this row-sequence dominance is distinct from the weak Bruhat order and
must not be reversed. The transposition criterion is
$$S=(a_1\,b_1)\cdots(a_m\,b_m)T$$
with $a_n<b_n$ and $b_n$ occupying an earlier row-reading node than $a_n$ in
$(a_{n+1}\,b_{n+1})\cdots(a_m\,b_m)T$ for each $n$.

For entries $r,s$ of one component define $r\to_Ts$ if they lie in the same row
and $s$ is strictly to the right of $r$; $r\downarrow_Ts$ if they lie in the
same column and $s$ is strictly below $r$; and $r\nearrow_Ts$ if $s$ is
strictly above and strictly right of $r$ (south-west is the reverse of
$\nearrow_T$). A **weak Bruhat graph edge** $T\xrightarrow{r}S$ requires both
tableaux standard, $S=s_rT$, and $r$ occupying an earlier row-reading node
than $r+1$. Equivalently $r+1\nearrow_Tr$, or $r$ lies in an earlier component
than $r+1$. In particular a same-row or same-column swap is NOT a standard
edge. A **terminal path** is a directed path in this graph, and $T$ is
$(r_1,\dots,r_m)$-**terminal** if there are standard tableaux
$S_1\xrightarrow{r_1}S_2\xrightarrow{r_2}\cdots\xrightarrow{r_m}T$.

The **Garnir belt** at a node $(a,b,n)$ with $(a+1,b,n)$ also a node of $\mu$
consists of the nodes $(a,c,n)$ for $b\le c\le\mu_a$ and the nodes
$(a+1,g,n)$ for $1\le g\le b$. The **Garnir tableau** of shape $\mu$ at
$(a,b,n)$ is the unique maximal standard $\mu$-tableau in the order $\unlhd$
among the standard $\mu$-tableaux agreeing with $t^\mu$ outside the
$(a,b,n)$-Garnir belt; it equals $t^\mu$ in the degenerate case
$b=1=\mu_a$. A **horizontal brick** is a string of consecutive entries along
same-row right arrows. For the vertical exceptional-prefix and terminal assertions assume that
$\mu$ is a multipartition; the rank, prefix-order and row-sorting assertions
allow multicompositions. The following source facts are retained with these
exact conventions and are proved below: the transposition criterion and the
prefix-shape criterion; the row-strictness of a vertical consecutive swap and
its exceptional-prefix comparison; agreement outside the Garnir belt for
tableaux below a Garnir tableau; and the four terminal alternatives for a
horizontal or vertical consecutive pair, the last alternative being $t^\mu$
for a horizontal pair and the corresponding Garnir tableau for a vertical
pair. No choice.

In the situation of
[[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]]:

1. If $T\xrightarrow{\,r\,}S$ (i.e. both tableaux are standard, $S=s_rT$, and
$r$ occupies an earlier row-reading node than $r+1$, as in
[[def-tableau-domination-order-garnir-tableaux-and-bricks]]), then
$\deg(S)-\deg(T)=-a_{i_ri_{r+1}}$, where $i_T=(i_1,\dots,i_d)$ and $a$ is the
Cartan matrix of the regime.

2. More generally, if $w_T=s_{r_1}\cdots s_{r_m}$ is a reduced decomposition,
then $\deg(T)-\deg(t^\mu)=\deg\bigl(\psi_{r_1}\cdots\psi_{r_m}e(i_{t^\mu})\bigr)$
in the grading of [[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]].

3. If $T$ is the $(a,b)$-Garnir tableau with entry $r$ in the node $(a,b)$, and
$S$ is a standard $\mu$-tableau with $S\lhd T$ and $i_S=i_{s_rT}$, then
$\deg(S)-\deg(T)=-a_{i_ri_{r+1}}$ as well.

No choice is used.

For every commutative ring $R$, every $q\in R^\times$, and every partition
$\lambda\vdash n$ with row symmetrizer $m_\lambda=x_\lambda$, put
$m_{st}:=T_{d(s)}^*m_\lambda T_{d(t)}$ for standard $\lambda$-tableaux $s,t$,
where $d(t)\in D_\lambda$ is the element with $t^\lambda\cdot d(t)=t$. Then:

1. $\{m_{st}:\lambda\vdash n,\ s,t\in\operatorname{Std}(\lambda)\}$ is an
$R$-basis of $H$ (the **Murphy basis**), and $m_{st}^*=m_{ts}$.

2. The $R$-spans $I^{\unrhd\lambda}$ of $\{m_{uv}:\mu\unrhd\lambda\}$ and
$I^{\rhd\lambda}$ of $\{m_{uv}:\mu\rhd\lambda\}$ are two-sided ideals of $H$
(dominance order), and $I^{\unrhd\lambda}/I^{\rhd\lambda}$ is free with basis
the classes of $\{m_{st}:s,t\in\operatorname{Std}(\lambda)\}$.

3. The **Murphy cell module**
$C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda):=M(\lambda)/(M(\lambda)\cap I^{\rhd\lambda})$ is free
with basis $\{m_t:=x_\lambda T_{d(t)}+I^{\rhd\lambda}:t\in\operatorname{Std}(\lambda)\}$
and satisfies the **cell law**: for $h\in H$ and standard $s,t$,
$$m_{st}h\equiv\sum_{v\in\operatorname{Std}(\lambda)}r_v\,m_{sv}\pmod{I^{\rhd\lambda}},\qquad r_v\in R,$$
with coefficients $r_v$ independent of $s$.

4. There is a unique $R$-bilinear **Murphy form** $G_\lambda$ on
$C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)$ with
$m_{us}m_{tv}\equiv G_\lambda(m_s,m_t)m_{uv}\pmod{I^{\rhd\lambda}}$; it is
symmetric, associative in the sense
$G_\lambda(m_sh,m_t)=G_\lambda(m_s,m_th^*)$, and its radical is a submodule of
$C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)$.

5. The basis, the ideals, the cell law and the form are compatible with every
base change.

The proof also supplies the auxiliary identities used by the comparison:
$\tau(T_w)=\delta_{w,1}$ defines a trace with
$\tau(T_u^*T_v)=\delta_{u,v}q^{\ell(u)}$ (step 1.3); for a composition
$\alpha$ and the partition $\beta$ obtained by sorting its parts,
$x_\alpha=T_dx_\beta T_d^{-1}$ with a block-reordering permutation $d$
(step 2.2); and for the Garnir composition $\alpha$ at a node of $\rho$,
$x_\rho\sum_{d\in S_\alpha\cap D_\rho}T_d
=\sum_{v\in S_\rho\cap D_\alpha}T_v^*x_\alpha$ (step 2.3).
The block-reordering and Garnir data are specified in those steps.

In particular $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)$ is finite free of rank
$f^\lambda=|\operatorname{Std}(\lambda)|$. No choice principle is used.

Let $n\ge0$ be an integer, with $S_0=\{1\}$ as in
[[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]. Let $A:=\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1}]$ be the ring of Laurent polynomials in one
indeterminate $v$ over $\mathbb Z$. For $n\ge2$ the **generic type-A Hecke
algebra** $H_v(n)$ is the associative unital $A$-algebra presented by generators
$T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$ and the relations
$$T_i^2=(v-1)T_i+v\quad(1\le i<n),\qquad T_iT_{i+1}T_i=T_{i+1}T_iT_{i+1}\quad(1\le i\le n-2),\qquad T_iT_j=T_jT_i\quad(1\le i,j<n,\ |i-j|>1),$$
that is, the quotient of the free unital associative $A$-algebra on
$T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$ by the two-sided ideal generated by these relators. The
first relation is written in the **RG-13 quadratic normalization**
$(T_i-v)(T_i+1)=0$, equivalent to the displayed form over $A$. For $n\le1$ there
are no generators and we set $H_v(n):=A$.

**Standard basis elements.** Let $S_n=\operatorname{Sym}(\{1,\dots,n\})$ with
simple transpositions $s_i=(i\ i+1)$
([[def-symmetric-group]]), and let $w\in S_n$ have inversion length $\ell(w)=\ell$
([[def-weyl-group-and-length-for-finite-gl-n]]). Choose a reduced expression
$w=s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_\ell}$, that is, a word of the minimal length $\ell(w)$
representing $w$, and put
$$T_w:=T_{i_1}\cdots T_{i_\ell}\in H_v(n),$$
the empty product when $w$ is the identity of $S_n$, so that $T_w=1$ for that
element. That $T_w$ is independent of the chosen reduced expression, and that
the elements $T_w$ form an $A$-basis of $H_v(n)$, is proved in the
standard-basis theorem below
([[thm-standard-basis-of-the-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]]); the notation
distinguishes the generator $T_i$ with $1\le i\le n-1$ from $T_w$ for the group
element $w$.

**Specializations.** Let $R$ be a commutative $A$-algebra with structure map
$\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1}]\to R$, $v\mapsto v_0$, and suppose $v_0\in R^\times$. The
**specialization** of $H_v(n)$ at $v_0$ is the $R$-algebra
$R\otimes_AH_v(n)$; it is presented over $R$ by the images of $T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$
subject to the same relations with $v$ replaced by $v_0$, and we write $H_{v_0}(n)$
for it. Two specializations are used on this page: $v\mapsto1$, where the
quadratic relation becomes $T_i^2=1$ together with the braid and commutation
relations, and $v\mapsto q$, where $q$ is the prime power defining
$\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb F_q)$; the latter specializes the generic algebra to
the Hecke algebra attached to the finite general linear group. The condition
$v_0\in R^\times$ is part of the definition of a specialization and, for a nonzero coefficient ring $R$, excludes $v_0=0$. The zero ring
is allowed: its unique element is a unit and its specialization is the zero algebra.

In the generic type-A Hecke algebra $H_v(n)$ over $A=\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1}]$ with
generators $T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$, the quadratic relations
$(T_i-v)(T_i+1)=0$, the braid relations and the distant commutations, and with
$T_w$ the product of the $T_i$ along a reduced word for $w\in S_n$
([[def-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]]):

1. $\{T_w:w\in S_n\}$ is an $A$-basis of $H_v(n)$; in particular $H_v(n)$ is
free of rank $n!$ over $A$;
2. for every $w\in S_n$ and every $1\le i\le n-1$,
$$T_wT_i=T_{ws_i}\quad\text{if }\ell(ws_i)=\ell(w)+1,\qquad T_wT_i=(v-1)T_w+v\,T_{ws_i}\quad\text{if }\ell(ws_i)=\ell(w)-1,$$
where $\ell$ is the inversion length of $S_n$
([[def-weyl-group-and-length-for-finite-gl-n]]); consequently the rule rewrites
every monomial in the generators as an $A$-linear combination of the $T_w$.

No choice principle is used.

Let $F$ be a field, $q\in F^{\times}$, let $e=e(F,q)$ and assume $e>n$ (with $e=\infty$ allowed); let $\lambda\vdash n$, $H=H_{F,q}(S_n)$, and let $S^{\lambda}_{\mathrm M}$ be the Murphy cell module with Murphy basis $(m_t)_{t\in\mathrm{Std}(\lambda)}$ ([[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]]).

1. (**Separation**) If $s,t$ are standard $\lambda$-tableaux with $[\operatorname{content}_s(k)]_q=[\operatorname{content}_t(k)]_q$ for all $1\le k\le n$ then $s=t$. More precisely, if the q-content values agree for all $k\notin\{i,i+1\}$ for some $i$, then $s=t$ or $t=s(i\ i+1)$. 2. (**Idempotents**) Let $\mathcal R_k$ be the set of distinct q-content values of the entry $k$ over standard tableaux of **all** partitions of $n$. For a standard $\lambda$-tableau $t$ define $$F_t:=\prod_{k=1}^{n}\ \prod_{\substack{c\in\mathcal R_k\\        c\ne[\operatorname{content}_t(k)]_q}}        \frac{L_k-c}{[\operatorname{content}_t(k)]_q-c}\in F[L_1,\ldots,L_n].$$ These are orthogonal idempotents of $H$; their actions on $S_{\mathrm M}^\lambda$ project onto the corresponding simultaneous eigenlines. Put $f_t=m_tF_t$. Then $f_tL_k=[\operatorname{content}_t(k)]_qf_t$ and $f_t=m_t+\sum_{s\rhd t}a_sm_s$. The global content sets are essential for the asserted idempotency in $H$, rather than only the induced same-shape endomorphisms. 3. (**Orthogonal seminormal basis**) $\{f_t:t\in\mathrm{Std}(\lambda)\}$ is a basis of $S^{\lambda}_{\mathrm M}$ satisfying $f_tF_s=\delta_{ts}f_t$ and $\langle f_s,f_t\rangle_\lambda=\delta_{st}\langle f_t,f_t\rangle_\lambda$; it is the **seminormal basis** of the Murphy cell module. 4. (**Generator action**) Let $s$ be a standard $\lambda$-tableau, $1\le i<n$ and $t:=s(i\ i+1)$, and put $\rho:=\operatorname{content}_s(i)-\operatorname{content}_s(i+1)\in\mathbb Z$. If $i$ and $i+1$ lie in the same row of $s$ then $f_sT_i=q\,f_s$; if they lie in the same column then $f_sT_i=-f_s$; otherwise $t$ is standard and $$f_sT_i=\alpha_i(s)\,f_t-\frac{1}{[\rho]_q}f_s,\qquad \alpha_i(s):=\begin{cases}1,&s\rhd t,\\[1mm]\dfrac{[1+\rho]_q[1-\rho]_q}{[\rho]_q[-\rho]_q},&t\rhd s,\end{cases}$$ where $[-\rho]_q$ is the extended quantum integer of [[def-hecke-jucys-murphy-elements-and-q-contents]] and for the swapped tableau $\operatorname{content}_t(i)-\operatorname{content}_t(i+1)=-\rho$. No semisimplicity of $H$ is assumed and no choice principle is used.

derivations.claim: **The ordered Murphy subspaces over the universal ring.** First work with the ungraded level-one left Murphy cell $S_{\mathcal R}(\mu)$ at the universal Hecke parameter $u$, where $\mathcal R=\mathbb Z[u,u^{-1}]$. List all removable corners as $B_1,\ldots,B_b$ from bottom to top. Define $W_j^{\mathcal R}$ to be the span of standard $z_T$ with the maximal entry $d$ in $B_1,\ldots,B_j$. Each is a free basis-coordinate subspace, with free quotient. If $S\unlhd T$ in the tableau Bruhat order, its prefix of size $d-1$ dominates the corresponding prefix of $T$ by [F3]. For corners of a fixed partition, $\mu\setminus B$ dominates $\mu\setminus A$ exactly when $B$ is lower than or equal to $A$: subtracting a node from a lower row retains one extra node in every intervening upper-row prefix sum. Thus every standard tableau below $T$ has $d$ in the same or a lower corner. This is the direction needed for the bottom-to-top filtration.

**Prove stability generically and descend exact coefficients.** Extend scalars to $\mathcal K=\mathbb Q(u)$ and use the cell-level triangular eigenbasis of [F4]. Step 1.1 implies $W_j^{\mathcal K}=\operatorname{span}_{\mathcal K}\{f_T:d\text{ in }B_1,\ldots,B_j\}$: the triangular basis change and its inverse preserve each such set. For $1\le r<d-1$, the seminormal formula for $T_r f_T$ involves only $f_T$ and, when standard, $f_{s_rT}$. Both have $d$ in the same node, so every $W_j^{\mathcal K}$ is an $H_{\mathcal K,u}(S_{d-1})$-submodule. The action matrix of $T_r$ on the universal $z$-basis has coefficients in $\mathcal R$ by [F4]. Every coefficient exiting $W_j^{\mathcal R}$ vanishes after the injective extension $\mathcal R\hookrightarrow\mathcal K$, hence is zero already in $\mathcal R$. Therefore $W_j^{\mathcal R}$ is a submodule. This proves only stability of the ordered sums; it makes no claim that individual fixed-corner spans are stable after specialization.

**Identify the generic corner quotient on its standard vectors.** Fix $j$, put $A=B_j$ and $
u=\mu\setminus A$, and let $T_A$ be the standard filling with $d$ in $A$ and the remaining entries row-filled in $
u$. For any standard $T$ with $d$ in $A$, deletion gives $ ar T$ of shape $
u$. On the eigenbasis quotient $W_j^{\mathcal K}/W_{j-1}^{\mathcal K}$ the map $f_T\mapsto f_{ ar T}$ is an $H_{d-1}$-isomorphism: for every generator $T_r$, $r<d-1$, the two contents, same-row/column alternatives, standardness of the swap and relative prefix dominance are unchanged by deleting $d$; hence the two displayed seminormal action matrices in [F4] are identical. The tableau $T_A$ is dominance-maximal among tableaux with $d$ in $A$, since its deleted tableau is row-filled. Thus the triangular correction to $f_{T_A}$ has only tableaux with $d$ in lower corners, so $f_{T_A}+W_{j-1}^{\mathcal K}=z_{T_A}+W_{j-1}^{\mathcal K}$. The initial eigenvector of $S_{\mathcal K}(
u)$ is $f_{t^
u}=z_
u$. If the row-reading index of $A$ in $\mu$ is $k$, the permutation $w_{T_A}$ sends the initial entry $k$ to $d$ and shifts $k+1,\ldots,d$ down by one, and has length $d-k$. The factorization $w_T=w_{ ar T}w_{T_A}$ is length-additive: the $d-k$ inversions involving $d$ are fixed, and all other inversions are precisely those of $w_{ ar T}$. Therefore $z_T=T_{w_{ ar T}}z_{T_A}$, and the generic isomorphism sends $z_T+W_{j-1}^{\mathcal K}$ exactly to $z_{ ar T}$. This identifies the standardized quotient map, not just an unspecified generic module isomorphism.

**The integral and specialized deletion quotient.** Define the $\mathcal R$-linear basis map $W_j^{\mathcal R}/W_{j-1}^{\mathcal R}\to S_{\mathcal R}(\nu)$ by $z_T\mapsto z_{\bar T}$. Both source and target are free with these corresponding bases. For each finite Hecke generator, both action matrices have entries in $\mathcal R$, and step 3.1 makes their difference zero in $\mathcal K$. Injectivity of $\mathcal R\to\mathcal K$ therefore makes that difference zero over $\mathcal R$. This is an integral module isomorphism. Base change $u\mapsto\xi$ gives the exact Murphy restriction filtration and deletion quotients over the original field $F$, including singular finite-$e$ parameters and positive characteristic. Because every inclusion was a basis-coordinate inclusion with free quotient, these scalar extensions preserve the entire filtration and its quotients; no flatness assumption on $F$ is needed and no generic denominator is specialized.

**Pass to the selected homogeneous basis and establish the shift.** Return to the fixed graded Hecke–KLR presentation. Its homogeneous theorem [F1] gives a triangular change $v_T=a_Tz_T+\sum_{S\lhd T}a_Sz_S$, $a_T
e0$. Step 1.1 therefore identifies every specialized $W_j$ with the span of the selected $v_T$ having $d$ in $B_1,\ldots,B_j$, so $W_j$ is a graded submodule. To verify that the deletion isomorphism of step 4.1 is homogeneous, choose compatible reduced words $w_T=w_{ ar T}w_{T_A}$, which are reduced by step 3.1. The grading is independent of this selected-word change by [F1]. The triangular expansion of $v_{T_A}$ has only lower-corner terms besides its nonzero leading term, so its image under the ungraded deletion quotient is $a_Az_
u$ for a fixed scalar $a_A
e0$. The previous-rank generators have the same tower images under the transported KLR presentation: the inclusion keeps $X_r,T_r$ for $r<d$; hence its weight idempotent $e(\mathbf i)$ becomes $\sum_j e(\mathbf i,j)$, since both project onto the generalized eigenspaces of those same first $d-1$ commuting $X$ operators. The defining dot formula and fixed crossing normalizing series use only the same adjacent $X$ operators, so $y_r$ for $r\le d-1$ and $\psi_r$ for $r<d-1$ are unchanged. This is the tower transport in [F2], without assigning any simple-module shape from a JM tuple; consequently the deletion map sends $v_T+W_{j-1}=\psi_{w_{ ar T}}v_{T_A}+W_{j-1}$ to $a_Av_{ ar T}$. Rescaling the quotient map by $a_A^{-1}$ gives the homogeneous-basis correspondence. The degree recursion [F1] gives $\deg T=\deg ar T+d_A(\mu)$, so $W_j/W_{j-1}\cong S(
u)\{d_A(\mu)\}$ as graded modules. Other preferred words preserve the same graded subspaces and graded isomorphism by [F1]; no word-independence of the individual vectors is asserted.

**Select the removable-$i$-node filtration.** The residue projector $e(\alpha-\alpha_i,\alpha_i)$ on restriction selects exactly the homogeneous basis vectors whose last residue is $i$ by [F1, F2]. Apply this exact idempotent summand to the all-corner filtration of step 5.1. A quotient for a corner $B_j$ of residue different from $i$ becomes zero, while a quotient for an $i$-corner remains $S(\mu\setminus B_j)\{d_{B_j}(\mu)\}$. Removing the repeated zero steps leaves precisely the bottom-to-top sequence $A_1,\ldots,A_c$ of the Statement, with $V_m$ spanned by the selected $v_T$ whose last node is among $A_1,\ldots,A_m$. This proves the asserted filtration and all graded quotients. If there are no removable $i$-nodes the selected module is zero and the filtration is empty; rank zero has no restriction assertion. The entire argument uses finite bases, finite spectra and explicit scalar extension, so no choice principle or cellular head classification is used.

citations.quote:
Keep the notation of
[[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]]; the vectors
$v_T=\psi_{w_T}z_\mu$ may a priori depend on the chosen reduced decompositions
$w_T=s_{r_1}\cdots s_{r_m}$. Then:

1. For every $\mu$-tableau $T$ one has $v_T=\sum_{S\unlhd T}a_Sz_S$ with
$a_T\ne0$ when $T$ is standard; hence the standard vectors form a basis of
$S(\mu)$ triangular with respect to the standard basis $\{z_T\}$ of
[[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]].

2. If $w_T=s_{r_1}\cdots s_{r_m}=s_{t_1}\cdots s_{t_m}$ are two reduced
decompositions of the same $w_T$, then
$\psi_{r_1}\cdots\psi_{r_m}z_\mu-\psi_{t_1}\cdots\psi_{t_m}z_\mu=\sum_{S\lhd T,\ i_S=i_T,\ \deg S=\deg T}a_Sv_S$;
in particular the grading on $S(\mu)$ defined by $\deg(v_T):=\deg(T)$ is
independent of the choices.

3. For every $r$ the vectors $e(i)v_T$, $y_rv_T$ and $\psi_rv_T$ lie in
the prescribed homogeneous components; when nonzero their degrees satisfy
$$e(i)v_T=\delta_{i,i_T}v_T,\qquad \deg(y_rv_T)=\deg(y_r)+\deg(T),\qquad \deg(\psi_rv_T)=\deg(\psi_re(i_T))+\deg(T).$$
Hence $S(\mu)$ is a graded $R^\Lambda_\alpha$-module with homogeneous basis
$\{v_T\}$ and $q$-character
$\operatorname{ch}_qS(\mu)=\sum_{T\in\operatorname{Std}(\mu)}q^{\deg T}i_T$;
forgetting the grading recovers the ungraded cell module of
[[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]].

No choice beyond the finite selections of reduced decompositions is used; the
resulting graded isomorphism class is independent of them by (2).

Assume inherited AC [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the highest-weight, crystal and global-basis suppliers invoked below; the finite algebra transport introduces no additional choice.

In the regime of
[[def-nondegenerate-root-of-unity-level-one-hecke-regime]] (both branches (C0)
and (CP)), fixing an admissible normalising series, the blockwise graded
isomorphism $\rho_\alpha:R^\Lambda_\alpha\to H^\Lambda_\alpha$ of
`thm-brundan-kleshchev-blockwise-hecke-klr-isomorphism` with the grading of
`cor-cyclotomic-hecke-blocks-inherit-a-nontrivial-z-grading` transports the
standard homogeneous cyclotomic data to the Hecke side, block by block and then
by the restricted direct sums of
[[def-graded-module-and-projective-grothendieck-groups-for-klr-towers]]:

1. the unique $A$-module isomorphism

Assume the Axiom of Choice [[def-axiom-of-choice]]. For the standard homogeneous graded quotient over any field, with arbitrary real symmetrizable Cartan datum and admissible graded KLR parameters, there is a unique $U_A$-module isomorphism $\phi:K_0(\mathrm{Proj}\,R^\Lambda)\to V_A(\Lambda)$ sending $1_\Lambda$ to $v_\Lambda$ and intertwining all normalized $E_i,F_i,K_i$ and divided powers. In particular $K_0$ is free over $A$. On the NEGATIVE half the vacuum map has exact kernel
$$\ker(U_A^-\to K_0(R^\Lambda))=\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{s>\lambda_i}U_A^-F_i^{(s)}.$$
This is the integral negative-half presentation; neither a full-$U_A$ quotient by only $F_i^{(\lambda_i+1)}$ nor invertibility of divided-power factorials is asserted.
For projectives, the tensor form $T(P,Q)=\mathrm{gdim}(P^\psi\otimes Q)$ transports to the highest-weight contravariant form normalized by $(v_\Lambda,v_\Lambda)=1$ and $\sigma(F_i)=q_i^{-1}K_iE_i$, $\sigma(E_i)=q_iF_iK_i^{-1}$, $\sigma(K_i)=K_i$. It is not the generic negative-half Lusztig form with a newly alleged radical.

For the same standard homogeneous general-field/general-Cartan parameters as
the integral projective theorem, the tensor pairing
$T(P,M)=\operatorname{gdim}(P^\psi\otimes M)$ is weightwise perfect and
$A$-bilinear, with normalized cover/simple dual bases. Its associated map
$$\Psi_{\mathrm{can}}:G_0(R^\Lambda)\longrightarrow V_A(\Lambda)^\vee=\bigoplus_\beta\operatorname{Hom}_A (V_A(\Lambda)_{\Lambda-\beta},A),\qquad \Psi_{\mathrm{can}}(M)(\phi(P))=T(P,M)$$
is an isomorphism to the RESTRICTED weight dual, identified inside
$V(\Lambda)$ using the highest-weight contravariant form. It intertwines the
CANONICAL module action having the same normalization as projective $K_0$, and
sends normalized simple classes to the form-dual projective basis. The KK
module action is also sound, but its intertwiner is
$\Psi_{\mathrm{KK}}|_\beta=q^{\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)}
\Psi_{\mathrm{can}}|_\beta$. Thus an unrescaled KK identification is not
asserted to send simples to the upper global basis. The Hom pairing is instead
first-bar-sesquilinear, $h(P,M)=T(P^\#,M)$; this does not alter the bilinear
tensor-dual identification.

Fix a finite integer $e \ge 2$ and charge $0$, with the independent-root affine
Cartan datum, its lattices and its diagram reflection $\tau$ fixed as in
[[def-cyclic-affine-type-a-cartan-datum]]: $I = \mathbb{Z}/e\mathbb{Z}$, simple
roots $\alpha_i$, fundamental weights $\Lambda_i$, $\delta$, and
$\tau(i) = -i$. A *node* is a pair $(r,c) \in \mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N}$, and
the *residue* of a node is $\operatorname{res}(r,c) := c - r \bmod e$; this is
the level-one, charge-$0$ specialization of the residue used in
[[def-residue-signature-normal-good-conormal-and-cogood-nodes]]. We use the
English convention (rows increase downwards) and the node language of
[[def-removable-and-addable-nodes-of-a-partition]] and
[[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]].

A partition $\lambda$ is **$e$-regular** if every positive integer occurs as a
part of $\lambda$ fewer than $e$ times, and **$e$-restricted** if
$\lambda_a - \lambda_{a+1} < e$ for every $a \ge 1$, the sequence being padded
by trailing zeros; these are the prime-case notions of
[[def-p-regular-and-p-restricted-partitions]] with $e$ in place of the prime
$p$. A column of height $e$ is allowed in an $e$-restricted partition. The two
classes are exchanged by conjugation: $\lambda$ is $e$-restricted if and only if
its conjugate $\lambda'$ is $e$-regular (step 2.1 below).

**The modular (restricted) signature.** Let $\lambda$ be a partition and
$i \in I$. The $i$-nodes of $\lambda$ are its addable and removable nodes of
residue $i$; list them *top to bottom*, that is by increasing row index and then
increasing column index, obtaining $A_1,\dots,A_n$, and form the word
$\sigma = (\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_n)$ with $\sigma_m = +$ if $A_m$ is addable and
$\sigma_m = -$ if $A_m$ is removable. Whenever $r < s$ with $\sigma_r = -$,
$\sigma_s = +$ and $\sigma_{r+1} = \dots = \sigma_{s-1} = 0$, replace
$\sigma_r,\sigma_s$ by $0$; repeat until no $-$ lies above a $+$. The survivors
are the *normal* removable and *conormal* addable $i$-nodes; write
$\varepsilon_i(\lambda)$ and $\varphi_i(\lambda)$ for their numbers. If
$\varepsilon_i(\lambda) > 0$, the *good* $i$-node is the removable node
belonging to the first surviving $-$, and $\tilde e_i\lambda := \lambda$ with
that node deleted; if $\varphi_i(\lambda) > 0$, the *cogood* $i$-node is the
addable node belonging to the last surviving $+$, and $\tilde f_i\lambda$ is
$\lambda$ with that node added (otherwise the respective partial operator is
undefined). This is Kleshchev's reduced $i$-signature at charge $0$ and level
one, with good $=$ top normal and cogood $=$ bottom conormal. **This is the
reading used for the restricted (symmetric-group) model**, in which the labels
of the level-one basic module are the $e$-restricted shapes; Fayers' equivalent
formulation reads the list in reverse order, with the opposite cancellation, and extracts the
last surviving $- $ and first surviving $+$, and his increasing-column model of
the $e$-restricted labels is the basic crystal $B(\Lambda_0)$.

**The linear (symmetric-group) model and the transport $J$.** Let
$$F_{\mathrm{QG}} = \bigoplus_{\lambda} \mathbb{Q}(q)\,|\lambda\rangle$$
be the charge-$0$ level-one partition Fock space with
$\operatorname{wt}(|\lambda\rangle) = \Lambda_0 - \sum_i m_i(\lambda)\alpha_i$,
where $m_i(\lambda)$ is the number of nodes of $[\lambda]$ of residue $i$, and
with the declared finite node operators $F_i$, $E_i$, $K_h$, $K_d$ of
[[def-level-one-partition-fock-space-and-node-residues]] (the operators act on
*all* partitions). When the wedge bar $\psi$ is supplied by the global-basis
construction, transport it by the formula below; this convention does not
construct that bar. The **symmetric-group model** $F_{\mathrm{sym}}$
is the same $\mathbb{Q}(q)$-vector space with the basis relabelled
$M_\lambda := |\lambda'\rangle$; equivalently, $J : F_{\mathrm{sym}} \to F_{\mathrm{QG}}$
is the $\mathbb{Q}(q)$-linear isomorphism
$$J M_\lambda = |\lambda'\rangle \qquad (\lambda \text{ a partition}),$$
with the field map $q \mapsto q$ (not $q \mapsto q^{-1}$). Transport the
structure along $J$:
$$E_i^{\mathrm{sym}} := J^{-1} E_{-i}^{\mathrm{QG}} J, \qquad F_i^{\mathrm{sym}} := J^{-1} F_{-i}^{\mathrm{QG}} J, \qquad K_h^{\mathrm{sym}} := J^{-1} K_{\tau h}^{\mathrm{QG}} J \quad (h \in P^\vee), \qquad \psi_{\mathrm{sym}} := J^{-1} \psi J,$$
and give $M_\lambda$ the weight
$\operatorname{wt}(M_\lambda) := \Lambda_0 - \sum_i m_i(\lambda)\alpha_i$. The
transported operators are defined on the ambient basis of *all* partitions.
With $A := \mathbb{Z}[q,q^{-1}]$ and the local ring
$A_0 := \{\, f \in \mathbb{Q}(q) : f \text{ is regular at } q = 0 \,\}$, the
**standard chart** of the symmetric-group model is
$$(F_0)_{\mathrm{sym}} := \bigoplus_{\lambda} A_0\, M_\lambda ;$$
the full ambient model is indexed by all partitions, while its basic component
in this convention is carried by the $e$-restricted shapes (the comparison with
the QG model is made by the results of this page).

**Label dictionaries and boundaries.** The conjugation map $C : \lambda \mapsto \lambda'$
exchanges the $e$-restricted and the $e$-regular partitions, preserves the
addable/removable *type* of each node and negates residues; it is a comparison
map *between* the restricted and the regular models, not an involution of one
label set, and it is not the same-model sign (Mullineux) involution of
Kleshchev's Theorem 11.8, which fixes the restricted label set and negates
residues along a good-node path. In the symmetric-group regime (ground field of
characteristic $p > 0$, Hecke parameter $\xi = 1$, so that $e = p$ is prime) the
$e$-restricted partitions are the labels of the simple modules in the
dual-Specht convention and the $e$-regular partitions those of James, the two
dictionaries being related by
$D(\lambda) \cong D^{\lambda'} \otimes \operatorname{sgn}$, equivalently
$D^\mu \cong D(\mu') \otimes \operatorname{sgn}$ for $e$-regular $\mu$
([[prop-p-regular-and-p-restricted-simple-labels-are-related-by-conjugate-sign-duality]]);
for a general Hecke parameter the finite integer $e \ge 2$ is its quantum
characteristic (the smallest positive $e$ with $1 + \xi + \dots + \xi^{e-1} = 0$)
and need not be prime, so the general finite-$e$ crystal labels are not called
symmetric-group modules of "characteristic $e$". At quantum characteristic
$e = 0$ (no such positive integer exists, colors $\mathbb{Z}$) no finite affine
datum is present: every level-one partition is a crystal label, and no weight
formula or finite affine statement is made in this boundary.

Let $F:=\bigoplus_{\lambda}\mathbb Q(q)|\lambda\rangle$ be the charge-$0$ part of
the Fock space of
[[lem-semi-infinite-wedges-are-indexed-by-partitions-and-give-node-action-formulas]],
with basis indexed by all partitions and with the node operators $F_i,E_i$
defined by the stable finite-prefix action. Assign to $|\lambda\rangle$ the
**level-one weight**

$$\mathrm{wt}(|\lambda\rangle):=\Lambda_0-\sum_{i\in I}m_i(\lambda)\,\alpha_i, \qquad m_i(\lambda):=\#\{\text{cells of }\lambda\text{ of residue }i\},$$

where the **residue** of a cell in row $r$ and column $c$ is $c-r\bmod e$, and
the **size** $|\lambda|$ is the separate grading. The vacuum is the empty
partition $\varnothing$; $F_i$ adds and $E_i$ removes a node by the explicit
finite node formulas of the same item. The toral action is
$K_i|\lambda\rangle=q^{N_i(\lambda)}|\lambda\rangle$ with $N_i$ the
addable-minus-removable count, proved to be the Cartan pairing in
[[lem-the-node-count-is-the-level-one-cartan-pairing]], and
$K_d|\lambda\rangle=q^{-m_0(\lambda)}|\lambda\rangle$.

A partition is **$e$-regular** if each positive part occurs with multiplicity
$<e$, and **$e$-restricted** if $\lambda_r-\lambda_{r+1}<e$ for every $r\ge1$
(with $\lambda_{r}=0$ beyond the length). These operators are declared linear
endomorphisms here; the affine relations proved later establish the actual
module structure, so nothing about $F$ is silently assumed in this Definition.

Keep the conventions of the charge-$M$ Fock space
[[def-semi-infinite-q-wedge-fock-space-and-q-adic-topology]]. Normal wedges are
bijective with partitions through $i_k=M+\lambda_k-k+1$; in charge $0$ the
vacuum is the empty partition. The stable finite-prefix action defines linear
endomorphisms $F_i,E_i,K_i,K_d$ of $F^{(0)}$ by

$$F_i|\lambda\rangle=\sum_{\text{addable }\gamma\text{ of residue }i}q^{A_i^r-R_i^r}\,|\lambda+\gamma\rangle,\qquad E_i|\mu\rangle=\sum_{\text{removable }\gamma\text{ of residue }i}q^{-(A_i^l-R_i^l)}\,|\mu-\gamma\rangle,$$

where for $F_i$ the counts are taken in the smaller diagram $\lambda$ and count
addable/removable $i$-nodes strictly to the right of the added node (higher
content), and for $E_i$ the counts are taken in the smaller diagram $\mu-\gamma$
and count nodes strictly to the left of the removed node (lower content), with
the removed node excluded; all sums are finite. The toral operators act by
$K_i|\lambda\rangle=q^{N_i(\lambda)}|\lambda\rangle$ with $N_i$ the
addable-minus-removable count, and $K_d|\lambda\rangle=q^{-m_0(\lambda)}|\lambda\rangle$;
the size $|\lambda|$ is a separate grading. Charge $M$ replaces the residues by
content $+M$ and $K_d$ by $\Omega_M(d)-m_0$.

The constructed node operators on **all** partition vectors make the charge-$0$
partition Fock space $F$ into a $P$-graded integrable module for
$U_q(\widehat{\mathfrak{sl}}_e)$ with the fixed coproduct and the cyclic Cartan
datum: all toral commutation rules and mixed commutators
$[E_i,F_j]=\delta_{ij}(K_i-K_i^{-1})/(q-q^{-1})$ hold, and both quantum Serre
sums vanish, including the cubic $e=2$ case with
$a_{01}=a_{10}=-2$ and $[3]=q^2+1+q^{-2}$. Each color acts on finite Boolean
cubes, and $F_i,E_i$ change the $P$-weight by $\mp\alpha_i$. Ordinary standard
coefficients may have $q^{-1}$ poles; normalized Kashiwara lattice stability is
a separate statement.

Use the symmetric model $M_\mu=|\mu'\rangle$ of
[[def-symmetric-group-level-one-residue-and-partition-label-convention]], the
basic field subspace $V$ of the vacuum Fock space spanned by the restricted
lower vectors $G(\lambda)=\sum_\mu d_{(\lambda,\mu)}(q)M_\mu$ of
[[def-level-one-global-basis-transition-polynomials-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]],
and the bilinear form $B(M_\mu,M_\nu)=\delta_{\mu,\nu}$. Define the **standard
coordinate functional** $\operatorname{Std}_\mu$ in the restricted integral
weight dual of the lower lattice by
$\operatorname{Std}_\mu(x)=B(x,M_\mu)$. The restriction of $B$ to $V$ is
nondegenerate; identify its field dual with $V$ via $B$ and denote by
$\pi(M_\mu)$ the vector representing $\operatorname{Std}_\mu$, equivalently the
$B$-orthogonal projection of $M_\mu$ onto $V$. This is the definition of $\pi$
used below, not an undeclared projection from a generic upper-basis definition.
If $G^*(\lambda)$ is the $B$-dual upper vector, then
$$\operatorname{Std}_\mu=\pi(M_\mu)=\sum_{\lambda\ \mathrm{restricted}} d_{(\lambda,\mu)}(q)\,G^*(\lambda).$$
At each content the restricted $\operatorname{Std}_\lambda$ form an $A$-basis of
the upper dual lattice, by the restricted dominance-unitriangular coefficient
minor. The full family of raw $M_\mu$ is the basis of the ambient standard
lattice; the full projected family $\operatorname{Std}_\mu$ is generally
redundant. The projection $\pi$ need not land in the lower integral lattice. In
$e=2$ one has $G_{11}=M_{11}+qM_2$ and
$G_{11}^*=(M_{11}+qM_2)/(1+q^2)$, exhibiting the possible field denominator.
The sums at fixed content are finite. Choice is inherited only from the
declared global-basis suppliers.

Let $\lambda\in P$ be a dominant integral label weight, put
$m_i:=\langle\lambda,h_i\rangle\ge0$, and let $M(\lambda)$ be the quantum Verma
module with highest vector $v_\lambda$
([[def-quantum-verma-module-and-simple-highest-weight-quotient]],
[[def-kac-moody-integral-and-dominant-integral-weights]]).

(i) The quotient $\tilde L(\lambda):=M(\lambda)/\sum_iU_q(\mathfrak g)F_i^{(m_i+1)}v_\lambda$
is nonzero, has finite-dimensional label weights and support contained in
$\lambda-Q_+$, is integrable, and equals the canonical simple highest weight
module $L(\lambda)$, which is simple also as an ordinary (not assumed graded)
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module.

(ii) **Universality.** Every integrable cyclic highest weight module $V$ of
highest weight $\lambda$ with highest vector $v\ne0$ receives a
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module map $\tilde L(\lambda)\to V$ with
$\bar v_\lambda\mapsto v$, and this map is unique; every nonzero such $V$ is
isomorphic to $L(\lambda)$.

(iii) Its character equals the classical integrable highest weight character of
the explicitly regularized realization of the datum. No global
$\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-freeness and no crystal or global basis is used.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum with $a_{ii}=2$ for
all $i$ ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and let
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be its Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]). The **linear
contravariant anti-involution** $\sigma$ of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ is defined on
generators by

$$\sigma(q)=q,\qquad\sigma(K_h)=K_h,\qquad\sigma(E_i)=q_iF_iK_i^{-1},\qquad\sigma(F_i)=q_i^{-1}K_iE_i,$$

extended as an anti-algebra map, $\sigma(xy)=\sigma(y)\sigma(x)$. It is
$\mathbb Q(q)$-linear, preserves the torus (it does not invert it), and is an
involution (Verification, step 1.1). It is distinct from the semilinear
contravariant anti-involution $\tau$ with $\tau(q)=q^{-1}$,
$\tau(E_i)=F_i$, $\tau(F_i)=E_i$, $\tau(K_h)=K_{-h}$ of
[[lem-quantum-serre-relations-are-stable-under-the-chevalley-involutions]].

Let $\lambda\in P$ be dominant integral ([[def-kac-moody-integral-and-dominant-integral-weights]]),
so $\langle\lambda,h_i\rangle\ge0$ for all $i$, and let $(M,v_\lambda)$ be a
**normalized highest weight module**: $M$ is a $P$-graded type-one quantum
weight module ([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]) with
$v_\lambda\in M_\lambda$, $E_iv_\lambda=0$ for all $i$, and $M=U_q(\mathfrak g)v_\lambda$.
(The normalized simple highest weight module $L(\lambda)$ is the companion
construction later on this page; the present definition applies to any
normalized highest weight module, in particular to the Verma module and to its
simple quotient.)

A **contravariant form** on $(M,v_\lambda)$ is a bilinear form
$B\colon M\times M\to\mathbb Q(q)$ such that

(i) $B$ is symmetric: $B(u,v)=B(v,u)$ for all $u,v\in M$;

(ii) $B$ is **homogeneous** for the label grading: $B(M_\mu,M_\tau)=0$
whenever the two labels have different toral characters, that is, whenever
$\langle\mu,h\rangle\ne\langle\tau,h\rangle$ for some $h\in P^{\vee}$;

(iii) $B(v_\lambda,v_\lambda)=1$ (the normalization);

(iv) $B$ is $\sigma$-invariant: $B(xu,v)=B(u,\sigma(x)v)$ for all
$x\in U_q(\mathfrak g)$ and all $u,v\in M$.

Because $\sigma$ is $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear and fixes the torus, condition (iv)
is equivalent to the adjunction displays

$$B(K_hu,v)=B(u,K_hv),\qquad B(E_iu,v)=B(u,q_iF_iK_i^{-1}v),\qquad B(F_iu,v)=B(u,q_i^{-1}K_iE_iv),$$

for all $u,v\in M$, $h\in P^{\vee}$ and $i\in I$ (Verification, step 2.1).

For $\lambda$ dominant and $L(\lambda)$ the normalized simple highest weight
module, such a form exists, is unique, and is nondegenerate on $L(\lambda)$;
moreover distinct label-weight spaces with distinct characters are orthogonal
by (ii). Uniqueness is proved here (Verification, step 2.2), as is the
orthogonality; consequently, when the pairing separates $P$, the distinct
label-weight spaces of $L(\lambda)$ are orthogonal and the restriction of $B$
to each finite-dimensional label-weight space is nondegenerate (Verification,
step 4.1). The
existence, the identification of the radical on the Verma module and the
descent to $L(\lambda)$ are proved in the local Cartan-projection lemma
`lem-cartan-projection-constructs-the-quantum-verma-contravariant-form`, which
is the declared justification of this definition. That lemma is proved on this
page, and its statement is the supplier of the existence and nondegeneracy
clauses above; establishing those clauses is its content rather than a claim of
this definition.

For the STANDARD graded cyclotomic quotient over any field and any real

a LEFT $H^\Lambda_d$-module lying in the block $H^\Lambda_\alpha$.

For every standard $\mu$-tableau $T$
([[def-young-tableau-standard-tableau-and-shape]]) fix a reduced decomposition
$w_T=s_{r_1}\cdots s_{r_m}$ of the associated permutation and put
$z_T:=T_{w_T}z_\mu$, $v_T:=\psi_{w_T}z_\mu$ in the Khovanov--Lauda presentation
of `def-type-a-cyclotomic-specialization-of-the-qg-klr-algebras`. For a
removable $i$-node $A$ of a partition $\lambda$
([[def-removable-and-addable-nodes-of-a-partition]]) define
$$d_A(\lambda):=\#\{\text{addable }i\text{-nodes strictly below }A\}-\#\{\text{removable }i\text{-nodes strictly below }A\}$$
(equivalently in the level-one symmetric residue convention of the regime) and
define the **degree** of a standard tableau inductively by
$\deg(\varnothing):=0$ and, for $d>0$,
$\deg(T):=\deg(T_{\le d-1})+d_A(\mu)$ where $A$ is the node of $T$ containing
